newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Amylin undaunted by setback.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Amylin undaunted by setback.

text.p: Amylin Pharmaecuticals Inc on Monday said Wall Street had overreacted to results of two initial Phase III trials of its high-profile candidate drug for diabetes, pramlintide.

Amylin Chairman Howard Greene said he believed results of four other ongoing Phase III trials, expected in late 1998, would vindicate his drug, a hormone used along with insulin to control glucose levels and improve weight control.
Amylin's shares were down 6-11/16 to 8-3/16 early Monday trade, with investors registering disappointment with trial results released after the stock market's close on Friday.

Johnson & Johnson, Amylin's collaborator, has committed almost $120 million to developing pramlintide. Its shares were up 15/16 to 56-7/8, with J&J's vast size apparently insulating it from the market concerns.
One of the pramlintide trials described Friday, of patients with adult-onset type II diabetes, showed a statistically significant lowering of glucose after six months but not after 12 months.
The other trial, of patients with early-onset type I diabetes, showed statistically significant reduction of glucose levels and weight after 12 months.
